function: Learned beam-hopping time-slot allocation (D3QN reinforcement learning) and transmit power allocation (unsupervised DNN estimating spectral efficiency) maximizing energy efficiency of a LEO satellite system (pp. 5-8).
system: One LEO satellite at 600 km, 16 fixed beams, 4 active per slot, 2-6 users per beam, 2 GHz, 10 MHz, beam-gain antenna model; no RIS (pp. 3, 9).
method: D3QN (2 hidden layers, 512 nodes) trained by reinforcement learning for time slots; 4-layer unsupervised DNN (EE loss) estimates spectral efficiency, then power by matrix inversion (pp. 5-9).
data_channel: Own simulator: free-space path loss, log-normal shadowing (4 dB), Bessel beam pattern, random user deployments and Gaussian traffic; TR 38.811 cited only for slant-range geometry (pp. 3, 8-9, 16).
test_conditions: Training: 4000x6 episodes (D3QN), 10000x6 instances (UDNN); testing on 2000x6 independent deployments, elevations 40-90 degrees, 32-96 users, 1.15-1.4 Mbps; also uniform traffic and outdated shadowing (pp. 9-13).
baselines: Monotonic optimization with TR-IPM [14]; quadratic transform with TR-IPM [13]; proposed D3QN with conventional unsupervised-DNN power allocation of [25]-[27] (p. 9).
metrics: Energy efficiency (Mbps/W), outage rate, complexity order, execution time versus users (pp. 9-14).
complexity: Orders O(Psi_D3QN)+O(Psi_UDNN)+O(Psi_Inv) in layers and nodes, matrix inversion O(G K Mact^3) (p. 8); baselines' orders (Table III); execution time versus users, RTX 4090 (pp. 13-14).
openness: Code with user guide: github.com/dhkim3988/DNN_RA_BH_LEO.git (ref. [38], pp. 14, 16).
q1_support: p. 3: "the distance between the LEO satellite and the ground user k can be defined as [28]"; [28] is 3GPP TR 38.811 (p. 16), cited only for the slant-range geometry. The channel is free-space path loss with log-normal shadowing (Eqs. 1-2), a custom simulator. Missing: any statement that the channel follows TR 38.811.
q2_support: p. 9: "is used to ensure separation from the evaluation dataset" is a held-out part of the same data, which does not count. The sweeps over users, traffic distribution and outdated channel (pp. 11-13) never say whether the models were retrained or trained once. Missing: an explicit test in a scenario unseen in training.
q3_support: p. 9: "conventional UDNN-based power allocation framework [25], [26], [27]" is the earlier learned baseline; the non-learned baselines are monotonic optimization/TR-IPM and quadratic transform/TR-IPM; all are compared on EE and outage rate (Figs. 6-15, pp. 10-13).
q4_support: p. 8: "the proposed D3QN scheme has a complexity of" O(Psi_D3QN), with the UDNN and matrix-inversion orders; Table III and the execution times of Fig. 16 are on p. 13.
q5_support: p. 14: "the complete source code of the simulations, including a detailed user guide, is publicly available in [38]"; reference [38] gives github.com/dhkim3988/DNN_RA_BH_LEO.git (p. 16).
notes: Included as area 6: learned beam-hopping time-slot allocation (D3QN) and transmit power allocation (unsupervised DNN) for a LEO satellite system; the NTN rule keeps learned power and resource control in the physical layer and admits single-antenna links. For the reviewer, q1: TR 38.811 [28] is cited only for the slant-range formula (p. 3); the channel (free-space path loss, shadowing, beam pattern from [21]) is a custom simulator, so 0. q2: the traffic-distribution test (Gaussian to uniform, p. 12) and the user-number sweep (p. 11) do not say whether the DNNs were retrained or trained once, and the UDNN output size depends on the number of users (p. 7), so 0. q3: the learned baseline Prop.D3QN/Conv.UDNN pairs the proposed D3QN with the conventional UDNN of [25]-[27] (p. 9), which could be read as an ablation of the proposed UDNN; marked met because [25]-[27] are earlier published learned power-allocation designs. Tables I-III are not in the text extraction; they were read from the page images (pp. 9, 13).
